findings.evidence: (c) Purpose: choose from the list below. ... Tie-breaks: if the reader must decide or approve, it is a Request even when it also reports status; if a prior unanswered ask exists, Follow-up wins ... otherwise Status ... and FYI for other informational messages ... findings.fix: Keep the purpose order, but state one default and one escape: classify as Request when a decision is required, Follow-up when a prior ask is unanswered, Escalation only when impact, uncertainty and mitigation are all present, else FYI; name Status, thank-you, announcement and introduction as FYI variants rather than a second classification pass.

findings.evidence: NEVER write a vague subject such as "Quick question", "Update" or "FYI" alone: the reader cannot triage it and it is skipped or answered late.
findings.fix: Keep the Gotchas that defy assumptions (proposed dates read as commitments, unflagged placeholders get sent, internal links leak). Drop or fold the obvious triage warning into the subject rule in step 5 and record that removal.

findings.evidence: description: Draft or rewrite a professional email to a peer, stakeholder, manager or leadership using What-Why-How. Use for status updates, approval requests, escalations, follow-ups, or when the user only asks to make a message shorter, clearer or less defensive, even without the word email. Produces a subject and body to paste; never sends. Not for casual chat replies; a finished draft can be reformatted for Slack or Teams on request.
findings.fix: Draft or rewrite a professional email (subject plus What-Why-How body) to a peer, stakeholder, manager or leadership: status updates, approval requests, escalations, follow-ups, deadline extensions and replies to a received message. Use when the user only asks to make a message shorter, clearer or less defensive, even without the word email. Produces text to paste and never sends. Not for casual chat replies, and not for sending mail; reformat a finished draft for Slack or Teams only on request.
